messages.text: Brits Skupski, Hewett clinch respective US Open doubles, wheelchair titles

metadata.summary: There was double success for Britain at the US Open on Saturday, with Alfie Hewett regaining his wheelchair singles title and Neal Skupski finally claiming the men’s doubles crown.
metadata.content: US Open 2026: Brits Neal Skupski, Alfie Hewett clinch respective doubles, wheelchair titles at Flushing Meadows | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content US Open 2026: Brits Neal Skupski, Alfie Hewett clinch respective doubles, wheelchair titles at Flushing Meadows Britain’s Alfie Hewett regained his US Open wheelchair singles title with victory in Saturday’s final; compatriot Neal Skupski then clinched the men’s doubles title; watch US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, NOW and Sky Sports app Saturday 12 September 2026 20:20, UK Image: Britain's Neal Skupski (right) celebrates US Open doubles glory with playing partner Christian Harrison There was double success for Britain at the US Open on Saturday, with Alfie Hewett regaining his wheelchair singles title and Neal Skupski finally claiming the men’s doubles crown. Emotional Hewett burst into tears after beating Tokito Oda 6-0 7-6 (7-5) to deny the 20-year-old Japanese star a calendar Grand Slam. The 28-year-old, who was beaten by Oda in the finals of the French Open and Wimbledon this year, said: "It's taken lot of hard work, a lot of soul-searching at times, a lot of reflecting. "The Wimbledon pumping was a tough one to swallow. I definitely came away from that one with a lot of regret, took some time off and had a hard, long look in the mirror about who I wanted to be on the tennis court and how I wanted to show up. messages.text: Hull gets Nordqvist backing to lead out Europe again in Sunday singles

metadata.summary: Anna Nordqvist insists Charley Hull’s game is ‘right where it needs to be’ and has kept faith in the Englishwoman by sending her out first for Team Europe in the Sunday singles.
metadata.content: Solheim Cup 2026: Charley Hull backed by Anna Nordqvist to lead out Team Europe in Sunday singles at Bernardus Golf | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to content Solheim Cup 2026: Charley Hull backed by Anna Nordqvist to lead out Team Europe in Sunday singles at Bernardus Golf Charley Hull has lost three of her first four matches with Lottie Woad during the first two days; Team Europe tied 8-8 with Team USA heading into the Solheim Cup final day at Bernardus Golf; watch the Sunday singles live from 9am on Sky Sports Golf By Ali Stafford at Bernardus Golf Saturday 12 September 2026 21:23, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Saturday fourballs from the Solheim Cup, where Jennifer Kupcho pulled Team USA level with two brilliant birdies Anna Nordqvist insists Charley Hull’s game is ‘right where it needs to be’ and has kept faith in the Englishwoman by sending her out first for Team Europe in the Sunday singles. Hull has only returned 0.5 points from the four matches but will lead out Europe for the second successive Solheim Cup, two years on from thrashing Nelly Korda 6&4 at the same stage. The Solheim Cup veteran partnered Woad to two defeats on Saturday, suffering the joint-biggest foursomes defeat in history with a 6&5 thrashing by Alison Lee and Lauren Coughlin before a final-hole loss to Yealimi Noh and Andrea Lee.
